title: interviewer-rotation-and-competency-pairing-framework
content:
Purpose:
This is a working framework for rotating interviewers across candidate stages, pairing interviewers to core competencies, and giving lightweight calibration + onboarding for new panelists. Goal is to maintain signal quality, reduce interviewer fatigue, and speed up interviewer ramp without adding heavy ceremony.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to technical and cross-functional interviews (IC/manager).
- Assumes minimum interviewer pool size per role: 6 active interviewers for IC roles, 4 for manager interviews.
- Rotation must respect individual bandwidth and no more than 3 interviews/day per interviewer.
- Confidential: some notes reference candidate names in separate trackers; keep this doc sanitized.

High-level design:
1) Weekly rotation cadence:
   - Week runs Mon-Sun.
   - Interviewers opt into a 2-week slot (Slot A or Slot B) to ensure distribution and repeat exposure.
   - Each slot: 3–5 interviews allocated across days; assignment engine (simple sheet) weighs recent participation (+1) and competency coverage (-1) to pick next panel.

2) Competency pairing matrix (lightweight):
   - Rows: Interviewer name. Columns: Core competencies (Problem Solving, System Design, Coding, Behavioral, Leadership, Product Sense).
   - Values: Primary | Secondary | Shadow (e.g., Primary = strong rater, Secondary = supports, Shadow = learning).
   - Rule: Every interview panel should include at least one Primary rater for the interview's target competency and one Shadow where feasible (for development).

3) Interviewer roles on panel:
   - Lead Rater (Primary): owns score for the competency and writes feedback summary.
   - Supporting Rater (Secondary): provides corroborating observations and raises mismatch flags.
   - Shadow/Observer: new interviewer or raters learning the rubric; writes notes but not final score.

4) 30-60-90 quick onboarding for new interviewers (practical, <2 hours total):
   - Day 0 (pre-shadow): read condensed rubric doc (15 min), watch 10 min calibration clip (example interview + annotated notes).
   - Week 1 (shadow): sit on 3 interviews as observer (no scoring). Debrief with People Ops coach 20 min after first week.
   - Week 4 (paired): run 1 interview as Supporting Rater and get feedback from Lead within 48h.
   - Week 8 (independent): lead a panel as Primary with People Ops quality spot-check.

Calibration and quality checks:
- Monthly mini-calibration (30 min) per role family: 2 example recordings, 1 disagreement case, quick consensus on scoring language. Mandatory for all Primary raters.
- Quarterly cross-role calibration: compare System Design vs. Coding scoring drift (identify scale shifts).
- Spot-checks: People Ops listens to random 5% of panels and tags for feedback.

Scoring rubric (short form):
- Use a 1–5 scale with explicit anchors. Keep comments tied to anchors.
  5: Exceptional — exceeds expectations across most axes. Clear signals, provides trade-offs, strong communication.
  4: Strong — meets expectations with few gaps; one or two minor areas for growth.
  3: Solid — competent but some gaps; will need ramp in first months.
  2: Borderline — misses several signals; may not meet role baseline.
  1: Insufficient — lacks core signals; declines.
- Fast-check rubric mapping examples (for interviewers to memorize):
  - Coding: 5 = algorithmic clarity + optimal complexity + clear tradeoffs; 3 = solves but messy; 1 = stuck without progress.
  - Behavioral: 5 = visible ownership + sociability + nuanced reflection; 3 = decent examples, limited context.

Template: panel assignment note (what gets sent to interviewer):
- Candidate: <name> (redacted in shared docs)
- Role & level: Backend Engineer II
- Focus for you: System design + reliability tradeoffs (Primary)
- Prep: read resume + 10-min read of candidate notes, watch attached clip (if present)
- Logistics: 60 min panel: 30 coding/system, 15 behavioral, 15 buffer/debrief
- Rubric anchors attached: link to confluence snippet

Day-of checklist for interviewers:
- Confirm in calendar 24h prior.
- Read candidate notes within 30 min before interview.
- Have rubric PDF open and pre-populated score bullets (3 bullets).
- At end of panel, Lead Rater writes 3-sentence summary and final score within 2 hours.

Common failure modes & mitigations:
- Fatigue: cap interviews/day; rotate high-intensity slots; provide 20-min recovery blocks between panels for paired interviewers.
- Halo/contrast bias: enforce 'blind' timing—each rater records raw notes before seeing other scores.
- Score inflation: monthly calibration + review of mean score by interviewer; >=0.5 SD from mean triggers mentoring.

Operational artifacts (minimal):
- Rotations sheet (single source of truth): columns = week, slot, interviewer, capacity, competencies.
- Interviewer competency matrix document (editable).
- Short rubric cheat sheet PDF (for day-of).
- Calibration deck (templates + example anchors).

Open questions / TODOs (working items):
- Automate rotation weighting into the scheduler (people-ops to prototype a lightweight script).
- Define incentives for panelists (teammates prefer deferred comp or recognition?).
- Confirm Prime/Secondary ratio for small pools (<6 interviewers).

Notes to self (Avery):
- Pilot with backend-interviews for 6 weeks, measure candidate time-to-offer and interviewer NPS.
- Try pairing external hires as Shadows (build bench).

References & links:
- Confluence: HR-Interview-Playbook (linked above)
- Jira: PEOPLE-314 (rotation automation epic)

Quick annex: sample calibration script (for 30-min session)
1. Play a 7-min excerpt from a recorded interview (anonymized).
2. Each Primary rater marks a score independently (2 min).
3. Facilitator runs 10-min discussion to align language; document 1–2 wording fixes.
4. End with one action item per rater for next month.

End of doc — comments welcome.
